exchanges: Hey! Quick question to start: have you heard of the resplendent quetzal?
Yes, it's a stunning bird from Central America, famous for its long green tail feathers.
I'm going to Costa Rica in February mainly to see one. My birding club has been teasing me about it for months.
That's a fantastic goal. February is a good time, since it's breeding season and they're more active.
Good to know! My friend Tomás is coming, he's a wildlife photographer and he's bringing his Nikon with the giant lens.
A long lens will be perfect for birds high in the canopy.
He's carrying it on the plane like a baby lol.
Fair, that lens probably cost more than the flights.
Probably! Anyway, my mom wants weekly updates while I'm gone. She's very into pickleball right now and wants to tell me about her games in return.
Sounds like a fair trade, bird photos for match reports.
My stepmom Linda is the opposite, she's not into racquet sports at all. She does curling every Thursday.
That's underrated, it's harder than it looks.
She says the sweeping is a real workout.
It is, people are surprised how tired they get.
So where should we base ourselves for quetzals?
Monteverde and San Gerardo de Dota are the classic spots. San Gerardo is especially reliable.
Haruto from the club says San Gerardo for sure. He's seen like 600 species, so I trust him.
With that list, he knows what he's talking about.
He's retired, he used to be an air traffic controller, which he says is why he's good at spotting tiny things far away.
That's a very plausible skill transfer.
Ha, maybe. Then after that we want a few days on the coast.
The Osa Peninsula is wonderful for wildlife, or Manuel Antonio if you want easier access.
Osa sounds great. Is it hard to get to?
A bit, usually a small plane or a long drive, but it's worth it.
Ok we'll think about that. Oh, and my friend Anika lent me her binoculars for the trip.
That's generous. Good binoculars make a big difference.
She won't need them for a while anyway, she just accepted a job in Halifax and is busy packing up her apartment.
Big change. Hopefully the move goes smoothly.
She's nervous about the winters but excited.
Maritime winters are damp, but the coastline makes up for it.
Oh, I got something wrong earlier. Tomás shoots with a Canon, not a Nikon. He would be offended if he heard me.
Photographers do take their brands seriously. Good thing he didn't hear.
He really would lecture me.
I believe it.
Do I need any vaccines for Costa Rica?
Routine vaccines plus hepatitis A and typhoid are usually recommended. Check with a travel clinic a few weeks ahead.
Ok, I'll book that. My doctor's office has a travel clinic.
That makes it easy.
What about rain gear? February is dry season, right?
Yes, on the Pacific side, but the cloud forest can still be damp, so a light rain jacket is smart.
Got it.
You're well prepared.
I'm also bringing a field guide. Haruto said the Stiles and Skutch one is the classic.
It's a classic, though it's heavy. Some people use a phone app as a lighter backup.
I've got the Merlin app already.
Merlin's sound ID is very handy in the forest.
Tomás wants to try night tours too, for frogs. He's obsessed with the red-eyed tree frog.
Night tours are excellent for frogs, and the red-eyed ones are very photogenic.

questions.message: What sport is my stepmom into again?
Tomás uses a Nikon, doesn't he?
What was the name of that bird ID thing on my phone?
I really hope we see some frogs on the night walk.
